title: Places and directions
objectives: I can name common places in a Brazilian city.
I can ask where a place is and how to get there.
I can understand and give simple directions using vire, siga, atravesse and continue.
I can say where things are using perto de, longe de, ao lado de, em frente a, atrás de and entre.

example.pt: O banco abre às dez.
example.en: The bank opens at ten.

example.pt: A farmácia fica na esquina.
example.en: The pharmacy is on the corner.

vocabulary.note: Often means a supermarket. A street market is a feira.

example.pt: Eu vou ao mercado de manhã.
example.en: I go to the supermarket in the morning.

example.pt: A praça é perto da igreja.
example.en: The square is near the church.

example.pt: Eu vou para a rodoviária de táxi.

example.pt: O ponto de ônibus fica em frente ao banco.
example.en: The bus stop is across from the bank.

example.pt: A estação de metrô é longe daqui.
example.en: The subway station is far from here.

example.pt: O correio fica perto do mercado.
example.en: The post office is near the supermarket.

example.pt: O hospital é grande.
example.en: The hospital is big.

example.pt: A igreja fica ao lado da praça.
example.en: The church is next to the square.

example.pt: Eu vou ao parque no domingo.
example.en: I go to the park on Sunday.

vocabulary.note: Brazilians say shopping for a mall; plural is shoppings.

example.pt: O shopping fica longe do centro.
example.en: The mall is far from downtown.

example.pt: A minha rua é tranquila.
example.en: My street is quiet.

example.en: Cross the avenue.

vocabulary.note: In São Paulo people also say sinal.

example.en: The bank is on the right.

example.pt: A farmácia fica à esquerda.
example.en: The pharmacy is on the left.

example.pt: Siga em frente por duas quadras.
example.en: Go straight ahead for two blocks.

example.pt: Meu trabalho é perto de casa.
example.en: My work is close to home.

example.pt: A rodoviária é longe do centro.
example.en: The bus station is far from downtown.

example.pt: Vire na segunda rua.
example.en: Turn onto the second street.

example.pt: Siga em frente até o semáforo.
example.en: Go straight ahead until the traffic light.

example.pt: Atravesse a praça e vire à esquerda.
example.en: Cross the square and turn left.

example.pt: Continue até a esquina.
example.en: Continue until the corner.

vocabulary.note: Agrees with the noun: a primeira rua, o primeiro semáforo.

example.en: Turn onto the first street on the right.

example.pt: A farmácia fica na segunda quadra.
example.en: The pharmacy is on the second block.

example.pt: O banco é o terceiro prédio.
example.en: The bank is the third building.

vocabulary.note: Ficar is the usual verb for the location of a fixed place.

example.pt: Onde fica o correio?
example.en: Where is the post office?

vocabulary.note: Brazilians say chegar em or chegar na: como eu chego na praça?

example.pt: Como eu chego na estação de metrô?

dialogues.title: Onde fica a farmácia?
dialogues.context: Kate is a visitor in Curitiba. She stops a man on the street to ask for help.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.pt: Com licença, onde fica a farmácia?
lines.en: Excuse me, where is the pharmacy?

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Fica na Rua das Flores, perto da praça.
lines.en: It's on Flores Street, near the square.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.pt: Como eu chego lá?
lines.en: How do I get there?

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Siga em frente por duas quadras. Depois vire à direita.
lines.en: Go straight ahead for two blocks. Then turn right.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.pt: Siga em frente e vire à direita. Entendi.
lines.en: Go straight ahead and turn right. I understand.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: A farmácia fica ao lado do banco.
lines.en: The pharmacy is next to the bank.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.pt: É longe daqui?
lines.en: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: Não, é perto. Uns cinco minutos a pé.
lines.en: No, it's close. About five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Kate
lines.pt: Muito obrigada!
lines.en: Thank you very much!

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.pt: De nada. Boa sorte!
lines.en: You're welcome. Good luck!

dialogues.title: Ao telefone
dialogues.context: Tiago is at the subway station and is going to Luiza's apartment for the first time. He calls her for directions.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Oi, Luiza! Estou na estação de metrô.
lines.en: Hi, Luiza! I'm at the subway station.

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.pt: Oi, Tiago! Atravesse a avenida e continue em frente.
lines.en: Hi, Tiago! Cross the avenue and keep going straight.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Tá. Atravesso a avenida e sigo em frente.
lines.en: Okay. I cross the avenue and go straight.

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.pt: Depois vire na segunda rua à esquerda.
lines.en: Then turn onto the second street on the left.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: A segunda rua à esquerda. E depois?
lines.en: The second street on the left. And then?

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.pt: Meu prédio fica em frente ao mercado.
lines.en: My building is across from the supermarket.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Está entre a padaria e a escola?
lines.en: Is it between the bakery and the school?

lines.speaker: Luiza
lines.pt: Isso! É o prédio azul.
lines.en: That's it! It's the blue building.

lines.speaker: Tiago
lines.pt: Já vejo o mercado. Chego em cinco minutos!
lines.en: I can already see the supermarket. I'll be there in five minutes!

dialogues.title: No ponto de ônibus
dialogues.context: Paula waits at a bus stop in the center of town and asks another passenger, Rui, for help.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: Moço, esse ônibus vai para a rodoviária?
lines.en: Excuse me, does this bus go to the bus station?

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Vai, sim. Ele passa pela praça e pelo hospital.
lines.en: Yes, it does. It goes past the square and the hospital.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: A rodoviária é longe do centro?
lines.en: Is the bus station far from the center?

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Não, é perto. Fica atrás do shopping.
lines.en: No, it's close. It's behind the mall.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: E onde fica o ponto para o metrô?
lines.en: And where is the stop for the subway?

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Fica ali, ao lado da igreja.
lines.en: It's there, next to the church.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.pt: Obrigada, moço!
lines.en: Thanks!

lines.speaker: Rui
lines.pt: Imagina. O ônibus chega logo.
lines.en: Don't mention it. The bus is coming soon.

grammar.title: Ir and estar: movement and location
grammar.explanation:
Use ir (to go) for movement and estar (to be) for where you are right now. Ir is irregular: eu vou, você vai, nós vamos, vocês vão. Estar you already know: eu estou, você está.

To say where you are going, use ir para or ir a. In everyday Brazilian speech para is very common and is often shortened to pra: eu vou pra escola. Ir a is slightly more formal and is common with short trips and in writing: eu vou ao banco. Brazilians also say eu vou no banco in casual speech, although teachers prefer ao. To say where you are, use estar em: eu estou no banco, ela está na praça.

Note the difference between going to a place and being in it. Eu vou ao mercado means I am heading there. Eu estou no mercado means I am already there. When you give the means of transport, use de: eu vou de ônibus, but eu vou a pé when walking.

examples.pt: Eu vou ao banco agora.
examples.en: I'm going to the bank now.

examples.pt: Ela vai para a rodoviária de táxi.
examples.en: She goes to the bus station by taxi.

examples.pt: Nós estamos na praça.
examples.en: We are in the square.

examples.pt: Vocês vão pra escola a pé?
examples.en: Do you all walk to school?

examples.pt: Meu pai está no correio.
examples.en: My father is at the post office.

grammar.title: Contractions: do, no, ao, pelo
grammar.explanation:
When the prepositions de (of, from), em (in, on, at), a (to) and por (through, by) meet the articles o, a, os and as, they join into one word. This is not optional: you always say no banco, never em o banco.

De and em simply add the article: de + o = do, de + a = da, em + o = no, em + a = na. A joins with the article too: a + o = ao and a + a = à, with a written accent. The accent on à is called crase and it marks that two a sounds have merged: vou à farmácia. Por + o = pelo and por + a = pela.

The preposition para also has a casual contraction in speech: para + o = pro and para + a = pra, as in eu vou pro banco. These are spoken forms and are fine in informal writing. Contractions do not happen with a or de in front of a name without an article: eu vou a Curitiba, eu sou de São Paulo.

examples.pt: Eu moro perto do mercado.
examples.en: I live near the supermarket.

examples.pt: Ela está na farmácia.
examples.en: She is at the pharmacy.

examples.pt: Vou ao parque com meus amigos.
examples.en: I'm going to the park with my friends.

examples.pt: O ônibus passa pela avenida.
examples.en: The bus goes along the avenue.

examples.pt: Eles vão às lojas no sábado.
examples.en: They go to the stores on Saturday.

grammar.title: Prepositions of place
grammar.explanation:
To say where something is, combine a place word with a preposition. The most useful ones are perto de (near), longe de (far from), ao lado de (next to), em frente a (in front of, across from), atrás de (behind), entre (between) and em cima de (on top of).

Most of them end in de or a, so they contract with the article that follows: perto do banco, longe da praça, ao lado do mercado, atrás da igreja, em frente ao hospital, em frente à escola. Entre does not contract: entre a padaria e a escola.

Use ficar or estar for location: a farmácia fica ao lado do banco. Ficar is the more natural verb for places that do not move, such as buildings, streets and cities. Use estar for people and things that can move: o Pedro está atrás da porta. To ask, say onde fica...? or onde é...? Both are common in speech.

grammar.title: Giving directions with commands
grammar.explanation:
When you give directions in Brazil, you use the command form for você. It looks like the third person singular, but the ending is flipped: -ar verbs end in -e and -er and -ir verbs end in -a. So virar becomes vire, atravessar becomes atravesse, continuar becomes continue, and seguir becomes siga. You do not say the word você in a command.

Put the direction after the verb: vire à direita, vire à esquerda, siga em frente, atravesse a avenida. To say where to turn, use na plus an ordinal: vire na primeira rua, vire na segunda à esquerda. Ordinals agree with the noun: o primeiro semáforo, a primeira rua, a segunda quadra, o terceiro prédio.

To ask for help, use com licença before a question. Moço and moça are polite ways to get a stranger's attention. Useful questions are onde fica...? and como eu chego...? Brazilians usually measure distance in quadras and minutes on foot: fica a duas quadras, fica a cinco minutos a pé.

examples.pt: Vire à direita na esquina.
examples.en: Turn right at the corner.

examples.pt: Siga em frente por duas quadras.
examples.en: Go straight ahead for two blocks.

examples.pt: Atravesse a praça e vire à esquerda.
examples.en: Cross the square and turn left.

examples.pt: Continue até o semáforo.
examples.en: Continue until the traffic light.

examples.pt: Vire na terceira rua à direita.
examples.en: Turn onto the third street on the right.

culture.title: Streets, blocks and asking for help
culture.text:
Brazilian addresses start with the type of street, then the name and then the number, for example Rua das Flores, 120 or Avenida Paulista, 1000. People measure short distances in quadras, which means blocks, and in minutes on foot. In Brasília, a city planned from scratch, addresses use letter-and-number codes for residential blocks, and many visitors ask for directions to a quadra rather than a street.

It is normal to ask a stranger for directions. Start with com licença and use moço or moça to get their attention. Brazilians are usually happy to help, but be careful with the answer fica logo ali, which literally means it is right over there. It can mean anything from a few steps to several blocks, so ask for more detail if you are not sure.

Most people now use apps such as Waze or Google Maps to move around, but asking someone in person is still common. The word rodoviária refers to the main intercity bus terminal, which in many cities is the central point for traveling to other towns, because long-distance buses are the main form of public transport between cities in Brazil.

exercises.prompt: Match the Portuguese with the English
How do you ask 'Where is the pharmacy?'
exercises.explanation: Onde means where. Ficar is the usual verb for the location of a place.
Vire is the command for virar, to turn. Esquerda is left.
Em + o = no, em + a = na, em + os = nos, em + as = nas.
Atrás de means behind. Ao lado de is next to.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'the second street'?
exercises.explanation: Rua is feminine, so the ordinal is also feminine: segunda.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'The bank is next to the pharmacy'?
choices: O banco fica em frente à farmácia.
O banco fica atrás da farmácia.
O banco fica longe da farmácia.
O banco fica ao lado da farmácia.
exercises.explanation: Ao lado de means next to.

exercises.prompt: Which verb does the command 'siga' come from?
exercises.explanation: Seguir means to follow or to go along. Siga em frente means go straight ahead.

exercises.hint_en: Today I am going to the supermarket.
exercises.explanation: Ir: eu vou, você vai, nós vamos.

exercises.explanation: Em frente a + o = em frente ao. In casual speech you also hear em frente do.
Virar becomes vire in the command form.

exercises.prompt_pt: A casa dele fica ___ a padaria e a escola.

exercises.explanation: Entre means between and does not contract.
